A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Safety Mirage research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLaVA safety, over-prudence, and utility experiments in Section 6, with additional attack, coreset, visual-perturbation, and saliency results in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and A1–A3 and the accompanying experimental figures.

M1.justification: The one-word attack procedure, RMU and NPO adaptations, and composite retain objective are identical in Sections 4–5 and Appendix C.

E1.justification: Both versions use VLGuard, SPA-VL, MM-SafetyBench, FigStep, VQAv2, TextVQA, ScienceQA, and VizWiz, with the same textual attacks and visual-perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding main and appendix experiments, including original LLaVA, Unsafe-Filter, Mixed-SFT, and Posthoc-SFT. The revised background citations do not change evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The same 7B/13B models, full and LoRA fine-tuning settings, attack-shot protocols, ASR/RR/accuracy metrics, and Qwen judging procedure appear in both versions. Appendix training and evaluation settings also match.

E4.justification: Attack-shot sensitivity, response decomposition, GCG evaluation, token saliency, coreset trade-offs, and visual-perturbation analyses are retained unchanged, including their appendix results and examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including Figure 7's rejection-probability boxplots. Neither version introduces additional run/seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical entries and qualitative findings match, including Tables 1–3 and A1–A3 and Figures 1–7 and A1–A5. Rendered comparison confirms that the experimental displays are identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations in Equations 1–4 and A1–A2 and their definitions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about spurious correlations, one-word jailbreaks, over-prudence, and mitigation through machine unlearning.

C2.justification: Explanations of rejection shortcuts, unlearning's response mechanism, safety–utility trade-offs, and visual robustness are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same model-scale and benchmark-coverage limitations.

D1.justification: Appendices C and D retain identical hyperparameters, hardware, training settings, filtering details, and judging prompt. The abstract's code-access statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 replaces citations to MIMIC-IT and Gao et al. (2023) with three Zhang et al. works on viewport prediction, TAMM for 3D shape understanding, and monocular 3D detection. MIMIC-IT leaves the bibliography; Gao's LLaMA-Adapter V2 remains cited in Section 1. The substantive safety/unlearning positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp and citation suffixes change, including BLIP-2 from 2023b to 2023a and RAIN from 2023c to 2023b. Narrative wording and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Citation edits alter Section 2's line wrapping and reflow reference entries across pages 12–15. Scientific figures and tables retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement.

improvement.justification: v5 makes a limited background-citation revision and associated presentation edits. The scientific argument, methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
